texts.Name: Anton Dziatkovskii
texts.What’s the most absurd place: Hacker News 'Who is hiring' threads. Plain-text comment dumps, zero formatting, no images - yet founders explain their architecture there more honestly than on most landing pages (your own post taught me more about the BPF runtime you're building than a docs page would). It works because the constraint strips the marketing away: one paragraph, a real engineer's voice, an audience made entirely of builders. I apply the same lesson daily - I run my multi-machine Claude agent fleet in public and write its operating manual as I go (110 public repos, flagships: claw-consensus, verbatim-citation-gate), and the rawest write-ups are consistently the ones engineers actually respond to.
